text:
B: Hello! Oh, hiya, you must be Kulwinder.
A: Yes. Hello.
B: I'm Nicola, lovely to meet you. I loved your kitchen in the photo, by the way, that calendar with all the dates on. You look so organised.
A: It's just the calendar from the grocer's. Otherwise I forget everything.
B: Well, it worked on me. Where are you?
A: Hayes. You?
B: Lancaster. Erm, do you work, or...?
A: Not now. I was a tailor. My hands, arthritis. And my back.
B: Oh, back. I know all about backs. Mine went in twenty-three, lower back and hip. I was a picture framer, and standing at the mount cutter all day just finished it off.
A: Workroom did my back. Bent over a machine twenty years.
B: Have they got you on a physio sheet as well? I do mine every single morning.
A: Every morning. Before anyone's up.
B: Same! Before the kettle, otherwise I talk myself out of it.
A: Mm. So you're arty, then. The prints on your wall.
B: Guilty. Lino prints, I do them at my kitchen table. And I'm doing an art history degree with the Open University. I know it's not everyone's cup of tea.
A: It's not mine, to be honest. Galleries. I don't get it. Someone puts a chair in a room and people stand round it.
B: Ha! Do you know, some of it I don't get either. But a good print, a good bit of fabric, it's the same thing, really, isn't it? You know when a hem sits right.
A: That's different. A hem has a job.
B: That's fair. Can I ask you something, actually, as a tailor? I sell vintage clothes on Vinted, bits I find in charity shops. I got this wool coat for four quid last month, gorgeous, but the lining's torn all down the back. Is that worth fixing?
A: Is the wool good? Moth?
B: No moth. Lovely heavy wool, nineteen-seventies, I think.
A: Then yes. You don't patch it, you replace the whole lining. If you patch it, it pulls, and it'll go again by the shoulder. People always patch. Then it looks cheap and you can't sell it for what it's worth. A proper lining, that coat is maybe sixty, seventy pounds.
B: Seventy! Oh, I'd have put it up for twenty-five.
A: Don't. It's a good coat, you said.
B: I couldn't do a full lining, though. I'd make a mess.
A: I'm thinking of doing alterations from home. When my hands are better. Not yet.
B: Well, if you ever do, I'd send you every coat I find. Honestly. I'd pay properly.
A: You're in Lancaster.
B: There's a post office!
A: Ha. Haan, maybe. We'll see.
B: I mean it, you know. People pay a fortune for vintage that's been done right.
A: Most people don't know what done right is.
B: You'd be amazed what customers notice, though. When I was framing—
A: Is that the bell?
